name: Abu al-Baqa' al-Rundi
bio: Salih ibn Yazid ibn Salih ibn Sharif al-Nafzi al-Rundi, known as Abu al-Baqa' and also as Abu al-Tayyib, was an Andalusian poet from Ronda, of the Berber tribe of Nafza, born in Muharram 601 AH (1204 CE). A jurist versed in arithmetic and the law of inheritance, he wrote on inheritance, on prosody and, in al-Wafi fi Ilm al-Qawafi, on the craft of verse, besides maqamas and ascetic poems. He often travelled to Granada to praise its rulers and seek their favour, and spent some months in Malaga attending the lessons of Ibn al-Zubayr, while the biographer Ibn Abd al-Malik called him the last of the men of letters of al-Andalus. He died in 684 AH (1285 CE); in the words of the historian Muhammad Abdallah Inan, his elegy for al-Andalus has kept his memory alive to this day.
